text: She rose slowly from her chair and came close to him, so close that he could see the light in her eyes, and she stood there waiting, as though she still expected something from him. <break time="0.8s" /> Marcher, however, only gazed at her in wonder, understanding nothing, and the moment for which she had perhaps been waiting all those years passed without a single word from him. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a spasm of pain crossed her face, her maid hurried in to help her away, and before he could grasp what had happened, Marcher found himself standing alone in the room. <break time="0.8s" /> When he was allowed to see her again some days later, she told him, in a voice that was hardly more than a whisper, that the thing he had waited for had already come. <break time="0.8s" /> It has come, he cried, bewildered, and she replied that it had indeed come and gone, that it lay behind him now, and that he had simply failed to recognize it. <break time="0.8s" /> I would have liked to live for you still, she said at last, with great tenderness, but I cannot, and not long after that last meeting May Bartram died. <break time="0.8s" /> Marcher was left with the bewildering knowledge that his fate had somehow already been decided, and with the bitter fact that the only person who could explain it was gone forever.
